text:
sam: seeing a burst of apiserver 5xx in ap-northeast-1 starting ~03:14 UTC, correlates with GPU autoscaler churn overnight. apiserver logs show repeated 'etcdserver: request timed out' and watch reconnect floods. :grimacing:
cheng: yup saw that alert. controlplane CPU ok but apiserver latency spikes to 800-1200ms on list/watch calls. lots of 429/503 for watch endpoints.
maria: any rolling upgrades or maintenance windows? didn't see planned changes.
sam: no planned. scale events from gpu-pool-autoscaler: ~120 nodes removed over 10m due to preemptible reclaim + some retry storms from job-scheduler.
oncall-sre: ops-bot fired an incident on watch-fanout backpressure. posted diagnostics: ops-bot: ALERT apiserver.watch.backpressure ap-northeast-1 03:14:22 -> 03:16:04 :fire:
ops-bot: top symptoms: etcd grpc timeouts, apiserver watch handler queue growth, controller-manager leader-election retries increased. attached tmp logs (snip).
seb: can you paste the kube-apiserver flags? we want to check --max-requests-inflight and watch-cache settings.
sam: minimal flags from node: --max-requests-inflight=400 --max-mutating-requests-inflight=200 --watch-cache-size=1000 --request-timeout=1m
cheng: watch-cache-size looks low given our scale and watch fanout. when controlplane sees lots of node churn the apiserver does re-list then watch resyncs for controllers, which spikes etcd QPS.
maria: also curious if etcd compaction/backpressure coincided. pinged infra to pull etcd metrics.
oncall-sre: from etcd: leader 1 had elevated raft apply duration ~>50ms and backend commit lag ~>200ms at the spike. disk iops for the etcd shard didn't show obvious saturation but queue length moved.
seb: quick mitigations: 1) throttle scale down for GPU pool during controlplane high-load windows 2) increase apiserver --request-timeout to 2m to avoid aggressive cancel 3) bump watch-cache-size and add more etcd client connections from apiserver (careful with fd limits) 4) temporarily pin critical controllers to other regions?
sam: can we patch autoscaler to respect a controlplane-load signal? avoid scale-down if apiserver latency > 200ms.
heng-dev: (reacting) we can add softbackoff in autoscaler, but need prod test.
cheng: recommended immediate actions: snapshot: scale down cooldown from 10m -> 30m for gpu-pool in ap-northeast-1, add a temporary guard: if apiserver watch-error-rate > 1% then block aggressive node deletes. then follow with apiserver tweak during low traffic window.
maria: I'll open a quick PR to autoscaler with these guards, tag infra and controlplane.
oncall-sre: ops-bot created incident: INC-2026-3123. assign to sam + cheng.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for autoscaler change (sha: b3f2a) to ap-northeast-1/gpu-pool (3 nodes)
sam: thanks. after deploy we should watch etcd leader metrics and apiserver watch-error-rate. also schedule an oncall takeover to keep manual throttles if needed.
seb: long-term: consider adding a small cold pool of non-preemptible GPUs to absorb churn, or move some heavy watchers to a dedicated cluster/aggregate layer to reduce fanout. cost vs reliability trade-off.
maria: noted. I'll add proposed cost calc: 3-5 non-preemptible GPUs vs expected cost of incidents.
cheng: logging action items: 1) bump cooldown and guard in autoscaler (PR+canary) 2) monitor apiserver --watch error-rate dashboard 3) evaluate watch-cache tuning and client conn limits 4) run controlled scale-down test during maintenance window 5) cost analysis for cold pool.
oncall-sre: tagging postmortem required if incident escalates. for now status: mitigation in canary, monitoring.
sam: update in 10m with metrics. thanks all :thumbsup:
